## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Kakusandhabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 24) is a canonical poetic narrative situated in the *Buddhavaṁsa* collection of the late Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Rendered in English as *The History of the Buddha Kakusandha*, the work chronicles the life, enlightenment, and ministry of Kakusandha, the first Buddha of the current fortunate eon (bhaddakappa) and one of the predecessors of Gotama Buddha [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records two modern translations of the text in two languages [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 340 matching passages across 27 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial reuse appears in its canonical commentary, the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā* (117 matches, including a contiguous segment spanning §20.1–26.4), along with secondary occurrences in the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Due to the highly formulaic structure of biographical accounts in the *Buddhavaṁsa*, substantial verse runs are also shared with adjacent accounts of past Buddhas, including the *Koṇāgamanabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 25), the *Kassapabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 26), and the *Sikhībuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 22) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments by DharmaNexus also associate segments of the text with Sanskrit Buddhist narrative traditions, particularly the *Mahāvastu-avadāna*, as well as Tibetan translations of texts such as the *Bhadrakalpikā-sūtra* (D0094) and the *Jātakanidāna* (D0032) [DharmaNexus].
